newsitem.title: LEBANON: 30 percent of Lebanese live below poverty line.
newsitem.headline: 30 percent of Lebanese live below poverty line.

text.p: About 30 percent of Lebanese people live below the poverty line, Social Affairs Minister Estefan ad-Douwaihi said in remarks published on Friday.
"There are studies estimating that 30 percent of the population live below the absolute poverty line but this estimate is not final," he said in a speech on Thursday.
Douwaihi, speaking at a meeting marking the inauguration of the International Year for the Eradication of Poverty, said a main reason was Lebanon's 1975-90 civil war.
"Lebanon has especially suffered in this context because of the Lebanese war at all social and economic levels," he said.
Most affected were small farmers, wage labourers, the displaced, the disabled, widows and orphans, he said.
"This suffering is manifested in the inability of these sectors to meet their essential and necessary needs of food, clothes, health, education and housing," Douwaihi added.
The government of Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri has been accused of ignoring the poor in its multi-billion dollar postwar rebuilding drive.

Ross Mountain, representative of the United Nations Development Programme, told the meeting that estimates showed that 28 percent of Lebanese lived in "relative poverty and that extreme poverty seems rare".
